clue.text: Making progress or making a bust?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: shaping a sculpted head out of metal in a smithy

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the phrase: to forge is to shape metal, and a bust is a sculpted head, so forging a head is making a bust.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge ahead is an idiom for advancing steadily or gaining ground.

clue.text: Pitiful choice of letters to complete the word COI ED

wordplay.words: choice of letters to complete the word COI ED
wordplay.note: the gap can be filled by F (coifed), L (coiled) or N (coined)

explanation.surface: A word game asks which letters fill the gap in COI ED, and the solver finds the choices sad.
explanation.walkthrough: The choice is written out as words: F OR L OR N.
explanation.definitionFit: Forlorn means sad and abandoned, so it can stand for pitiful.

clue.text: Ransack fund-raiser if legislators accept that

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to search through and steal from
second meaning, a political jibe: a gun counts as a money-spinner when lawmakers take gun-lobby cash

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic jab at gun-lobby donations to American lawmakers: the gun brings in the funds.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a drawer is to search it hastily for valuables, which is ransacking; the noun is a long-barrelled gun.

clue.text: Hurtful hormone takes time to grow at first

indicators.note: a word that takes something in holds it inside itself

parts.note: the hormone that controls blood sugar
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of grow

explanation.surface: A hurtful hormone needs time before its growth begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The time letter sits inside the hormone, splitting it after INSUL, and the G is tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulting means offensive or wounding to someone's feelings, which is hurtful.

clue.text: A delay held up fancy event

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means lifted and read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A posh party is late getting started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' looks like a synonym of delayed, but it is the signal to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive, formal celebration, so it is a fancy event.

clue.text: Along with Beethoven's Fifth, dancing a minuet is something you can study

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about into a new order
the fifth of a word is its letter in fifth place

parts.note: the fifth letter of Beethoven
taken as written, then rearranged with the letter before

explanation.surface: Beethoven's Fifth Symphony and a dancing minuet: a music student's syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Fifth suggests the symphony, but it is just the fifth letter of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanities are the academic subjects such as literature, history and philosophy, a field you can take at college.

clue.text: Pests sustaining a traveler underground

indicators.note: in a down clue, sustaining means holding up from beneath, so this piece goes below the other

parts.note: taken as written; the a in the definition is reused
lice are parasitic pests

explanation.surface: Vermin keep a passenger going on the subway.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice went down the rabbit hole into Wonderland, which makes her a traveler underground; 'underground' tempts toward the subway.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's heroine fell down a rabbit hole and journeyed beneath the earth in Wonderland.

clue.text: Teach lit differently — that's a kind of scholarship

indicators.note: done differently means put in another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A professor is urged to teach literature in a new way, as a branch of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: Scholarship suggests academic study, but here it is the money a college gives a student.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletic scholarship is a college award given for sporting ability, so athletic names one kind.

clue.text: One out of seven miners eyes New Zealand inappropriately

indicators.note: arranged inappropriately means not put in the proper order

parts.note: taken as written
NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand

explanation.surface: A miner leers at New Zealand in an unseemly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneezy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White, who work as miners.

clue.text: Failure leads us into genuine rejection

indicators.note: one thing going into another means it sits inside it

parts.note: genuine means real

indicators.note: the leading part of a word is its opening letter, so only the start is taken

parts.note: first letter of Failure
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's flop is put down to a sincere refusal by the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failure leads' reads as failures causing something, but leads only picks out the first letter of Failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a turning down of an offer or request, which is what a rejection is.

clue.text: 1,000 + 0 = 10 (just add water)

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
the zero reads as the letter O
an equals sign is read aloud as 'is'
the number written out

explanation.surface: A nonsense sum, with a recipe-style tip in brackets as if it were instant soup.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole equation is read as words: M, O, IS, TEN. The bracketed instruction is the definition, the way a packet says just add water.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something is to make it damp, which is exactly what adding water does.

clue.text: Romeo heading to the back — and beginning to yawn, too

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is added on here
the head of a word moving to the rear means its first letter is shifted to the end

parts.note: Romeo is the archetypal lover
first letter of yawn

explanation.surface: A dull Romeo drifts to the back of the room, and starts to yawn as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo here is not the NATO letter R but Shakespeare's lover: LOVER with its L moved to the end gives OVERL, then Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly and too both mean excessively, as in overly long or too long.

clue.text: Support and exceed in honesty?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to form the basis of
second meaning, read as two parts: to fib less than someone else

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as UNDER-LIE: to tell fewer lies than another person is to beat them for honesty, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To underlie is to lie beneath something as its foundation, so it means to support or underpin.

clue.text: Half the world is into marijuana at this point

indicators.note: going into another word means sitting inside it

parts.note: hemp is cannabis; it wraps the next piece
taken as written
here means at this place or point

explanation.surface: A claim that half the planet now uses cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemisphere is either half of the globe, divided at the equator or a meridian.

clue.text: Careless fellow pursues Elgin, losing his marbles?

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the other
someone who has lost his marbles has gone crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Lord Elgin, who removed the Parthenon sculptures known as the Elgin Marbles, is pictured carelessly losing them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elgin Marbles are the Greek sculptures in the British Museum, so 'losing his marbles' sounds like history, but it is the scrambling signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means failing to take proper care, a plain synonym of careless.

clue.text: Spilling a mug with cola can generate disease

indicators.note: spilling things scatters them, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that knocking over a mug of soda can make you ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaucoma is an eye condition in which raised pressure damages the optic nerve.

clue.text: Guard barring Sunday admission

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so something is left out

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A guard turns people away from a building that has no Sunday opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Guard looks like the definition, with the rest describing what he does; in fact SENTRY loses the S of Sunday, and admission is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry and admission both mean the right or act of going in.

clue.text: Period of atonement starts late, with the period we inhabit following

indicators.note: a word that starts late has lost its opening letter

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of penance before Easter
the era we live in is our age

explanation.surface: A season of repentance begins later than usual, followed by the modern age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like the instruction to place OUR AGE after, and it does that job, but it is also the definition, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity's following is the group of attendants around them, their entourage.

clue.text: Ape cut fruit

indicators.note: a cut word has been trimmed, here losing its final letter

parts.note: a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: An instruction to mimic someone slicing up a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Ape tempts as a verb meaning copy, but it is the noun: the great ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Orang is a short form of orangutan, the red-haired great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Veteran foiled a person disregarding the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and following letters

explanation.surface: An experienced gambler thwarts someone who ignores the betting odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds' sounds like betting, but it means the odd-numbered letters, which are thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: An old pro is someone with long experience in a field, which is what a veteran is.

clue.text: The same iodine reduction: one calorie

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
making a dent in something is reducing it
the Roman numeral for one
cal is the standard abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: A nutrition label reports that a dose of iodine, cut down, comes to one calorie as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iodine reduction' reads as one phrase, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike, so it can stand in for 'the same'.

clue.text: Three parts of a hospital for a woman giving birth?

parts.note: first part: a lab, where tests are run
second part: OR, the operating room
third part: ER, the emergency room

explanation.surface: Which three hospital departments serve an expectant mother?
explanation.walkthrough: A worker is the usual sense, so the question mark flags the pun: a woman in labor is a laborer.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman giving birth is said to be in labor, so she is jokingly a laborer.

clue.text: Fool holding court? Thanks, that should fix just about anything

definitions.text: that should fix just about anything

indicators.note: something holding another thing has it inside, so the outer word wraps the rest

parts.note: a dupe is someone easily fooled; the word wraps the next two pieces
CT is the abbreviation for court
ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: A jester at a royal court is thanked for a remedy that cures every problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is a British way of saying thank you. The definition is a descriptive phrase for the silver tape famed as a fix-all.
explanation.definitionFit: Duct tape is the strong cloth-backed adhesive tape proverbially used to patch up almost anything.

clue.text: Mark a carrier (formerly fashionable)

parts.note: TWA, Trans World Airlines, was a US airline that no longer flies
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: Someone singles out an airline that used to be trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is a first name here: Mark Twain wrote Huckleberry Finn, so the surname completes the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is the pen name of Mark, the American author Samuel Clemens, so the first name points to the surname.

clue.text: Excellent puzzle piece in enigmatic rebus

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
something enigmatic is puzzling and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; the P goes in among these letters before they are mixed

indicators.note: a piece of a word is a single part of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of puzzle

explanation.surface: Praise for a clever piece of a picture puzzle, set inside a baffling rebus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle piece' reads as a jigsaw piece, but it means only the first letter of puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is an adjective for something of the highest quality, a synonym of excellent.

clue.text: Ultimately, White Sox shortstop stole surgical boot

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so each word gives its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A Chicago White Sox shortstop steals a medical boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' and 'boot' suggest a theft of footwear; boot is the verb meaning to kick out.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot someone out is slang for to expel them.

clue.text: Speaking to take advantage of sheep

indicators.note: speaking means the words are said out loud, so the sound matters

parts.note: to take advantage of is to use

explanation.surface: Talk of exploiting the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewes are female sheep, so the plural answer stands for sheep.

clue.text: Rush around wildly and crash into a young attendant

parts.note: to ram is to crash into
a page is a boy attendant

explanation.surface: Someone charges about out of control and knocks over a pageboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush around wildly' looks like an anagram signal for the next words, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to run about in a violent, uncontrolled way.

clue.text: Packaging outspoken master of rhyme and rhythm

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: a hip-hop performer is a master of rhyme and rhythm

explanation.surface: A tribute to a forthright hip-hop star, with an odd word at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent W makes the two words sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is the paper or plastic covering a product, so it is packaging.

clue.text: El trains delivering the necessities for a future kind of travel?
